items.name: Claim

value.description: A property insurance claim submitted by a policyholder, from submission to decision.

items.rationale: The claim is the object being processed. The brief names the three required documents, the possible exception, the authority limit, automatic settlement of small claims, fraud referral and the decision deadline. The limits are recorded as booleans because their thresholds are not given (see q_authority_limit and q_small_claim).

items.name: Policy

value.description: The insurance policy a claim is checked against for eligibility.

items.rationale: The brief says the adjuster checks eligibility against the policy. The states and attributes are my reading.

items.name: ClaimDocument

value.description: A document submitted with a claim (photo, repair estimate, proof of ownership).

items.rationale: The brief lists the required document types. Tracking each document individually supports the evidence trail.
Eligibility is checked against the policy covering the claim.
A claim carries several required documents.

items.name: verify_documents

value.description: Confirm the required documents (photos, repair estimate, proof of ownership) are present, or that an exception has been granted, so the claim can be assessed.
requires: Claim.status == 'submitted' and ((Claim.photos_received == True and Claim.estimate_received == True and Claim.ownership_proof_received == True) or Claim.document_exception_granted == True)

items.rationale: The brief requires the documents before assessment and allows exceptions to the document rule.

items.name: grant_document_exception

value.description: Grant an exception allowing a claim to proceed without all the required documents.

items.rationale: The brief says exceptions to the document rule can be granted. Who grants them and on what grounds is not stated (q_exception_authority).
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: mark_eligible

value.description: Adjuster records that the claim is eligible under the policy.

items.rationale: The brief says an adjuster checks eligibility against the policy. Requiring an active policy is my reading.

items.name: mark_ineligible

value.description: Adjuster records that the claim is not eligible under the policy.

items.rationale: This is the negative outcome of the eligibility check.

items.name: refer_to_investigation

value.description: Flag suspected fraud and send the claim to the investigation unit.

items.rationale: The brief says suspected fraud always goes to the investigation unit.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: clear_investigation

value.description: The investigation unit finds no fraud and returns the claim for settlement.

items.rationale: The investigation needs a way back for claims cleared of suspicion. Returning to 'eligible' assumes eligibility was already confirmed or is confirmed by the unit (q_investigation_outcome).

items.name: reject_for_fraud

value.description: The investigation unit confirms fraud and the claim is rejected.

items.rationale: This is the outcome of a confirmed fraud investigation. It affects the claimant's rights and money, so it is subject to human review.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: settle_claim_automatically

value.description: Settle a small, eligible, non-suspicious claim without human intervention.
requires: Claim.status == 'eligible' and Claim.within_auto_settlement_limit == True and Claim.above_authority_limit == False and Claim.fraud_suspected == False

items.rationale: The brief says small claims can be settled automatically. The 'small' threshold is not given (q_small_claim).
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: approve_settlement

value.description: An adjuster or senior adjuster approves settlement of an eligible claim that is not settled automatically.

items.rationale: Claims that are not small, including those above the authority limit, still need a manual settlement path. Above the limit a senior adjuster must review (rule r_senior_review).
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: reject_claim

value.description: Reject a claim found ineligible under the policy.

items.rationale: This closes ineligible claims. It affects the claimant's rights, so a person decides.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: r_documents_before_assessment

value.description: Documents must be verified (or an exception granted) before eligibility is assessed.

items.rationale: The brief says a claim needs the required documents before it can be assessed.

items.name: r_documents_before_ineligible

value.description: Documents must be verified (or an exception granted) before a claim is assessed as ineligible.

items.rationale: Both assessment outcomes come after the document check.

items.name: r_senior_review

value.description: Settling a claim above the authority limit requires review by a senior adjuster.

items.rationale: The brief says claims above the authority limit need a senior adjuster. The limit value is unknown (q_authority_limit).

items.name: r_no_auto_settle_large_or_suspect

value.description: Automatic settlement is forbidden for claims above the authority limit, outside the small-claim limit, or suspected of fraud.
value.when: Claim.above_authority_limit == True or Claim.within_auto_settlement_limit == False or Claim.fraud_suspected == True

items.rationale: Only small claims may be settled automatically, and suspected fraud always goes to investigation.

items.name: r_no_settlement_while_suspected

value.description: No manual settlement while fraud is suspected.

items.rationale: The brief says suspected fraud always goes to the investigation unit.

items.name: r_exception_review

value.description: A person must approve any exception to the document rule.

items.rationale: Exceptions are allowed but the brief does not say who grants them. A senior adjuster is my assumption (q_exception_authority).

items.name: r_rejection_review

value.description: Rejecting an ineligible claim is decided by an adjuster, not autonomously.

items.rationale: A rejection affects the claimant's rights and money, so a person decides.

items.name: r_fraud_rejection_review

value.description: Rejection for fraud is decided by the investigation unit.

items.rationale: Suspected fraud goes to the investigation unit, and a fraud rejection affects the claimant's rights.

items.name: r_eligibility_access

value.description: Only adjusters and senior adjusters assess eligibility.

items.rationale: The brief says an adjuster checks eligibility.

items.name: r_ineligibility_access

value.description: Only adjusters and senior adjusters record ineligibility.

items.rationale: The brief says an adjuster checks eligibility.

items.name: r_investigation_access

value.description: Only the investigation unit concludes investigations.

items.rationale: Investigations belong to the investigation unit.

items.name: r_fraud_flag_write

value.description: Only adjusters, senior adjusters and investigators can change the fraud flag.

items.rationale: Protects the fraud routing from being bypassed.

items.name: claim_decided

value.description: Every claim reaches a decision: settled or rejected, within the committed deadline (5 or 10 working days, unresolved).

items.rationale: The brief's service promise is to decide every claim. The deadline itself is tracked through Claim.decision_due_at, not in the target.

questions.question: Is the decision deadline 5 working days or 10 days (working or calendar), and does it start at submission or when the documents are complete?
questions.why: The brief states both, and decision_due_at cannot be computed without it.

questions.question: What is the authority limit (amount and currency) above which a senior adjuster is required? Is it per claim or per adjuster?
questions.why: Rule r_senior_review depends on this threshold, and it is currently recorded as a boolean.

questions.question: What amount defines a 'small' claim eligible for automatic settlement? Is it the same as the authority limit or lower?
questions.why: Automatic settlement moves money without a person, so the limit must be explicit.

questions.question: Who may grant an exception to the document rule, and under what conditions? Which documents can be waived?
questions.why: The brief allows exceptions but names no decision-maker or criteria.

questions.question: Who may flag suspected fraud (adjusters, the automated agent, external fraud scoring), and what triggers suspicion?
questions.why: Fraud referral is mandatory, but its trigger is undefined.

questions.question: After an investigation clears a claim, does it return to eligibility assessment or straight to settlement? Can the investigation unit reject a claim, or does it advise an adjuster?
questions.why: This determines the clear_investigation and reject_for_fraud transitions.

questions.question: Can claims be partially settled (amount reduced by the deductible or coverage limit), or only settled in full or rejected?
questions.why: This affects the settlement actions and whether an approved amount must be recorded.

roles.name: adjuster
roles.description: Verifies documents, assesses eligibility against the policy, approves settlements within the authority limit, rejects ineligible claims and refers suspected fraud.

roles.name: senior_adjuster
roles.description: Reviews and approves settlements above the authority limit. Proposed as the approver of document exceptions, pending confirmation.

roles.name: fraud_investigator
roles.description: Member of the investigation unit who handles suspected fraud and concludes investigations.

agents.name: claims_intake_agent
agents.description: Checks whether the required documents are present and moves complete claims to assessment. It cannot grant exceptions.

agents.name: auto_settlement_agent
agents.description: Settles small, eligible claims not suspected of fraud, within the limits set by the rules. It refers suspected fraud to the investigation unit.

integrations.description: Reads the received photos, repair estimates and proofs of ownership attached to a claim.
Provides policy status, coverage limit and deductible for the eligibility check.
Issues the settlement payment for automatically settled claims (non-idempotent; needs duplicate protection).
Issues the settlement payment for manually approved claims.
Opens a case with the investigation unit for suspected fraud.

suggestions.note: descriptions only: roles are granted and systems are connected by an administrator

assumptions.statement: An active policy is required for a claim to be eligible.
Rejections affect claimant rights and are always decided by a person.
The three required documents are tracked as flags on the claim as well as individual ClaimDocument records.
A senior adjuster may also perform the actions of an adjuster.

unknowns: The small-claim threshold for automatic settlement
The applicable decision deadline (5 working days vs 10 days)
Who grants document exceptions and on what grounds
The fraud suspicion criteria and who can raise them
The payment system and how settlement is paid out

understanding.summary: Property insurance claims handling: a claim must have three required documents (photos, a repair estimate and proof of ownership) before assessment, unless a document exception is granted. An adjuster then checks eligibility against the policy. Claims within the automatic limit may be settled automatically. Claims above the authority limit need a senior adjuster. Suspected fraud always goes to the investigation unit. Every claim must be decided within a committed deadline.
understanding.outcome: Every claim is decided (settled or rejected) correctly and within the committed deadline, with the right level of human authority for large, exceptional or suspicious claims.
out_of_scope: Payment execution and accounting beyond recording the settlement decision
Fraud investigation methods and the investigation's internal workflow

Role grants and release approval belong to an administrator, and self-review would undermine the human reviews proposed here.
